title: Can turning a table stop the wobble?
hook: Can a turn help this square equal-leg table?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that on a gently uneven floor, turning a square table with equal legs by less than a quarter turn always reaches a position where all four feet touch

misconception: A wobbly table needs a wedge or a trimmed leg; turning it on the same floor cannot help.
objective: The illustrated signed gap crosses zero during a quarter turn. For square equal-leg tables on suitably gentle continuous ground, a balanced position exists.

claims.text: The illustrated signed gap crosses zero during a quarter turn. For square equal-leg tables on suitably gentle continuous ground, a balanced position exists.
claims.source: Baritompa, Löwen, Polster & Ross, Mathematical table turning revisited, full text opened 2026-10-14 at https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0511490. Square equal-leg table, continuous ground and slope/leg length conditions; proof of sign change and balanced position. Our cosine gap is an illustration, not a solution of the full contact geometry. claims.text: Four feet down is not level. Clear hot drinks before turning; steps, holes and unequal legs fall outside this model.

claims.text: Contact means the four feet touch the ground. It does not mean the tabletop is level. Equal legs and suitably gentle continuous ground belong to the stated model; unequal legs fall outside it.
claims.source: Baritompa, Löwen, Polster & Ross, Mathematical table turning revisited, full text opened 2026-10-14 at https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0511490. Square equal-leg table, continuous ground and slope/leg length conditions; proof of sign change and balanced position. Our cosine gap is an illustration, not a solution of the full contact geometry. Scenario values in the recall question are stipulated. Recall patch by learning-designer (session 2, 2026-10-14), applied by session 1. FC LH-3B (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): left unverified because the source could not be opened. The egress policy blocks arxiv.org and export.arxiv.org (proxy 403). Search-result abstract summaries agree: for equal-leg tables on continuous ground with bounded slope, a balanced position exists; balance is four-foot contact, not levelness. The keyed option is the only correct one; the why stays inside the stated model. Re-check from a connected host. See company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH3-2026-10-14.md (Batch B). | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Not verified on the source (arXiv math/0511490, unreachable here). Verified on its own terms: (1) four-foot contact does not imply a level top: an equal-leg table on a uniform inclined plane has all four feet down with the top tilted at the plane's slope, a counterexample. (2) The model statement matches the stage: WobbleStage inputs line "Equal legs · gentle continuous ground", caption "Not necessarily level."; spec limit "steps, holes and unequal legs fall outside this model". The keyed option ("It has stopped rocking; the top may still slope") is the only one consistent; "A table with one short leg would settle the same way" is outside the model. The existence of a balanced position (c1, already verified) is not part of this text.

recall.question: You turn a square equal-leg table on gentle, continuous ground until all four feet touch. What do you now know?
options: It has stopped rocking; the top may still slope
A table with one short leg would settle the same way
recall.why: Contact means the four feet touch the ground. It does not mean the tabletop is level. Equal legs and suitably gentle continuous ground belong to the stated model; unequal legs fall outside it.
